close_reason: Fixed in bf895d2: added rustdoc to ContactCard.created/updated and the four ContactCardFilterCondition date fields documenting the UTCDate format ('YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS[.SSS]Z') and the no-parse-validation contract inherited from jmap-types::UTCDate. Handler-layer rejection responsibility called out. The UTCDate parse-validation gap itself is a jmap-types property out of scope of this diff.
description:
The diff migrated six fields from `Option<String>` to `Option<UTCDate>`:
- ContactCard.created                    (card.rs:52)
- ContactCard.updated                    (card.rs:81)
- ContactCardFilterCondition.created_before  (card.rs:242)
- ContactCardFilterCondition.created_after   (card.rs:246)
- ContactCardFilterCondition.updated_before  (card.rs:250)
- ContactCardFilterCondition.updated_after   (card.rs:254)

The migration is correctly motivated (typed-newtype migration per
workspace AGENTS.md §"UTCDate" convention) and wire-format-identical
to the prior String shape. But `UTCDate` is a transparent String
newtype in `jmap-types` with no input validation:

```rust
let d: UTCDate = "not-a-date".into();             // accepted; no parse
let d: UTCDate = "2024-13-99T99:99:99Z".into();   // accepted; impossible date
```

The epic note (JMAP-glx8 NOTES) already flags this as inherited from
jmap-types and out of scope of this diff. But the contract risk now
extends to six previously-String fields:

1. A caller building a query in code via
   `filter.created_before = Some("2024-02-30T00:00:00Z".into())`
   compiles, serializes, deserializes, and the server returns garbage
   (no cards, or every card, depending on the backend's date parser
   leniency).

2. A server returning `card.created = Some("invalid".into())` produces
   wire data that round-trips through this crate but fails downstream
   typed date access (chrono::DateTime::parse_from_rfc3339, etc.).

The doc comment on ContactCard.created says only "Date and time when
the Card was created (UTCDateTime)." It does not:
- Link to `jmap_types::UTCDate`
- Describe the expected format (RFC 3339 §5.6, Z-suffixed)
- Warn that UTCDate accepts any string without validation

Minimum fix (in scope for this crate): rustdoc clause on each of the
six fields:

> Expected format: RFC 3339 §5.6 UTC timestamp (e.g.,
> `"2024-01-15T13:45:00Z"`). Note: [`UTCDate`] is a transparent
> String newtype and does NOT validate input at construction.
> Callers passing malformed strings will produce wire output that
> fails downstream typed date access (e.g., chrono parsing).

Stronger fix (out of scope of this crate; file against jmap-types):
add a `TryFrom<&str>` implementation to `jmap_types::UTCDate` that
validates RFC 3339 format. File as a separate bead under jmap-types.

Cross-reference:
- jmap-types UTCDate definition (presumably in src/lib.rs)
- AGENTS.md §"workspace conventions" — UTCDate convention
- RFC 9610 §3 created/updated fields
- RFC 8620 UTCDate type definition
title: ContactCard date fields inherit UTCDate's invisible validation contract; six new sites need format doc
